newsitem.title: USA: Repap debt drops post Avenor rejection.
newsitem.headline: Repap debt drops post Avenor rejection.

text.p: Bids for debt of Repap Enterprises Inc dropped as much as five points on Wednesday after shareholders of suitor Avenor Inc blocked a proposed acquisition, high-yield debt traders said.

The company's debt, including unit Repap Wisconsin 9-1/4 percent notes, was quoted at 97 bid, 100 offer compared with a 102 bid, 103 offer market prior to the vote. Only light selling in Repap debt was reported, however.

Avenor shareholders voted 74 percent against the proposal that featured one Avenor share for every eight Repap shares and the assumption of about $1.7 billion in debt. The bid, which was revised down from an earlier offer, excluded Repap's British Columbia operations.
Despite the poor bids, one high-yield debt analyst, who declined to be named, insisted the bonds had more upside than downside given the likelihood Repap will still find a buyer.

"The assets are still very good so there's little doubt in my mind that someone will come in and snap these things up," the analyst said. "They want to be sold; they're good assets; what more do you want."

Paul Greenberg, director of high-yield research at Bear, Stearns & Co Inc, said the severity of the negative vote may be due to shareholder interest in exploring a spurned Domtar Inc bid. Even if that does not occur, he said Repap may attempt to sell its assets individually.
Domtar on Wednesday reiterated its interest in a three-way merger with Avenor and Repap.
The downside is that there remains a "good chance of bankruptcy" for Repap, Greenberg said.
The companies are Canada-based paper and pulp concerns.
(( -- Al Yoon, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-859-1672 ))
